title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 — Mock Test 2
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (BioAsia 2026, retail inflation, C2S semiconductor programme, Arjuna Award 2026, RELIEF scheme expansion) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: In a code, 'PAINT' is written as 'RCKPV'. How is 'BRUSH' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +2: P→R, A→C, I→K, N→P, T→V. Apply to BRUSH: B→D, R→T, U→W, S→U, H→J ⟹ DTWUJ.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'CLOUD' is coded as 'DKPTE' (each letter shifts +1, -1, +1, -1, +1), how is 'SOLAR' coded?
questions.explanation: Pattern: +1, -1, +1, -1, +1. Apply to SOLAR: S+1=T, O-1=N, L+1=M, A-1=Z, R+1=S ⟹ TNMZS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A=1, B=2 ... Z=26, what is the SUM of letter values in 'TIME'?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, '129' means 'GO HOME EARLY', '157' means 'EARLY MORNING WALK', '264' means 'WALK FAST HOME'. What is the code for 'HOME'?
questions.explanation: 129 ∩ 264 = {2}. The common WORD between 'GO HOME EARLY' and 'WALK FAST HOME' is HOME. So HOME = 2.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'EARTH' is written as 'GCTVJ' (each letter shifts +2). Decode 'KQRGP' to find the original word.
questions.explanation: Shift each letter -2: K→I, Q→O, R→P, G→E, P→N ⟹ IOPEN.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the next term: B2C, D4F, F8I, H16L, ?
questions.explanation: Letters: B-D-F-H-J (skip 1, +2 each). Numbers: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 (×2). Last letters: C-F-I-L-O (+3 each). So next: J32O.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a girl, Aman said, 'She is the daughter of the only daughter of my mother.' How is the girl related to Aman?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Aman's mother = Aman's sister. So the girl is Aman's sister's daughter = Aman's niece.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: X is the brother of Y. Y is the daughter of Z. Z is the wife of W. How is W related to X?
questions.explanation: Y is Z's daughter. Z is W's wife → W is Y's father. X is Y's brother → X has the same parents as Y → W is X's father too.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A starts walking 7 km east, then turns left and walks 24 km. How far is A from the starting point?
questions.explanation: East 7, north 24. Distance = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man walks 3 km north, then 4 km east, then 6 km south, then 4 km west. Where does he end up?
questions.explanation: Net north = 3 − 6 = −3 km (i.e. 3 km south). Net east = 4 − 4 = 0. So he ends 3 km south of start.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If East becomes North-West, North becomes South-West, then what does South become?
questions.explanation: Each direction rotates 135° anti-clockwise. South + 135° anti-clockwise lands at North-East.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some doctors are engineers. All engineers are scientists.
Conclusions:
I. Some doctors are scientists.
II. All scientists are doctors.
questions.explanation:
I. Some doctors are engineers + all engineers are scientists ⟹ those doctors are scientists ⟹ some doctors are scientists. FOLLOWS.
II. Converse fallacy. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All cars are vehicles. No vehicle is wood.
Conclusions:
I. No car is wood.
II. Some vehicles are not wood.
questions.explanation:
I. Cars ⊂ vehicles, vehicles disjoint from wood ⟹ no car is wood. FOLLOWS.
II. Vehicles exist, none are wood ⟹ some vehicles (in fact all) are not wood. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some flowers are roses. All roses are red.
Conclusions:
I. Some flowers are red.
II. All roses are flowers.
questions.explanation:
I. Some flowers are roses, all roses red ⟹ some flowers red. FOLLOWS.
II. Converse — could be only some, not all. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: No book is a pen. Some pens are pencils.
Conclusions:
I. Some pencils are not books.
II. No book is a pencil.
questions.explanation:
I. Some pens are pencils; no book is a pen ⟹ those pens-which-are-pencils are not books ⟹ some pencils are not books. FOLLOWS.
II. Other pencils (not pens) might be books. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All keys are locks. Some locks are doors. All doors are gates.
Conclusions:
I. Some keys are gates.
II. Some locks are gates.
questions.explanation:
I. Keys are locks but only SOME locks are doors. The keys might not overlap with the door subset. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
II. Some locks are doors, all doors are gates ⟹ some locks are gates. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: A < B = C ≤ D; E > D; F = E
Conclusions:
I. F > A
II. C < F
questions.explanation:
I. F = E > D ≥ C = B > A ⟹ F > A. FOLLOWS.
II. F = E > D ≥ C ⟹ F > C ⟹ C < F. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five friends — V, W, X, Y, Z — sit in a row facing North. V sits at one end. W sits to the immediate right of V. X is between W and Z. Y sits at the right end. Where does Z sit?
questions.explanation: V@1 (left end). W@2 (right of V). Y@5 (right end). X between W(2) and Z, so X must be between positions 2 and Z. Remaining positions 3, 4 for X, Z. If Z@4 (third option index actually 4th from left = position 4): then X@3 (between W@2 and Z@4 ✓). So Z is 4th from left.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six people — A, B, C, D, E, F — sit around a circular table facing the centre. A is opposite D. B sits to the immediate right of A. C is between B and D. E is to the immediate left of A. F occupies the remaining seat. Who sits opposite C?
questions.explanation: A@1, D@4 (opposite). B@2 (immediate right of A). C@3 (between B and D). E@6 (immediate left of A). F@5. Opposite C(3) = seat 6 = E.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — P, Q, R, S, T — live on a 5-floor building (1=ground, 5=top). P lives below Q. R lives on floor 4. T lives on the top floor. S lives immediately above P. On which floor does P live?
questions.explanation: T=5, R=4. Remaining floors {1,2,3} for P, Q, S. S immediately above P → consecutive pair. P<Q. From {1,2,3}: P=1, S=2, Q=3 (P<Q ✓, S=P+1 ✓).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Four colleagues — A, B, C, D — were born in different months: February, April, June, August. B was born immediately before A. C was born before B. Who was born in February?
questions.explanation: C < B and B = A's predecessor. Months in order: Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug. Possible: C=Feb, B=Apr, A=Jun, D=Aug. C in February.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
What is the average age of A, B, C?
I. B = A + 4. 
II. C = 2A.
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: Together: A+B+C = A + (A+4) + 2A = 4A+4. Average = (4A+4)/3. Still depends on A. Insufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
On which day of the week did the meeting take place?
I. The meeting was held two days after the weekend ended.
II. The meeting was held on a working day.
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: From I: weekend ends on Sunday → 2 days after Sunday = Tuesday. ✓ Sufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many parallelograms can be formed using 4 horizontal lines and 5 vertical lines?
questions.explanation: Number of parallelograms = C(horiz,2) × C(vert,2) = C(4,2) × C(5,2) = 6 × 10 = 60.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
If P = +, Q = −, R = ×, S = ÷, evaluate:

12 R 3 P 18 S 6 Q 4
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the position of the Vice-President of India?
questions.explanation: Article 63 provides for the Vice-President of India.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: How many readings does a Bill normally undergo in each House of Parliament before being passed?
questions.explanation: A Bill is read three times in each House: First Reading (introduction), Second Reading (general discussion + clause-wise consideration), Third Reading (final passage).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
questions.explanation: Articles 23-24 deal with the Right against Exploitation, prohibiting human trafficking and child labour.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who is empowered to issue a writ for the enforcement of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226) can issue writs for enforcement of fundamental rights.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Amendment of the Indian Constitution lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who built the Qutub Minar in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began construction of the Qutub Minar in 1199 CE. It was completed by his successor Iltutmish.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The First Anglo-Mysore War was fought between the British and which Indian ruler?
questions.explanation: The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-1769) was fought between the British East India Company and Hyder Ali of Mysore.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant was the first woman President of the INC, in 1917 (Calcutta session). Sarojini Naidu was the FIRST INDIAN woman President (1925).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest (8,848.86 m) is the highest mountain peak in the world.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Cherrapunji' (Sohra) — known for some of the world's highest rainfall — is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Cherrapunji (officially Sohra) is in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent floods?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its devastating floods and frequent course changes.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which acid is found in lemon and other citrus fruits?
questions.explanation: Citric acid is the predominant organic acid in citrus fruits like lemon and oranges.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The unit of electric resistance is:
questions.explanation: The Ohm (Ω) is the SI unit of electric resistance, named after Georg Simon Ohm.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The Stapes (in the middle ear) is the smallest bone in the human body, ~3 mm long.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Plants prepare their food through which process?
questions.explanation: Plants synthesise glucose from carbon dioxide and water using sunlight via photosynthesis.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: In which year did India host the Cricket World Cup for the first time?
questions.explanation: India (jointly with Pakistan) hosted the Cricket World Cup for the first time in 1987 (Reliance World Cup).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: 'Yakshagana' is a traditional theatre form associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is a traditional folk theatre form of coastal Karnataka, combining dance, music, dialogue, and costume.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which dance form originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and was traditionally performed by Devadasis?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and was traditionally performed by Devadasis.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: 'Khelo India' is a flagship initiative under which Ministry?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.explanation: Khelo India is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive sports culture in India at grassroots level.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who became the first woman to be appointed as the Finance Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Nirmala Sitharaman became the first woman to be appointed as a full-time Finance Minister of India in 2019. Indira Gandhi held the portfolio briefly in 1970-71.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Where was BioAsia 2026 held, with the theme 'TechBio Unleashed — AI, Automation and the Biology Revolution'?
questions.explanation: BioAsia 2026 was organised by the Government of Telangana with Hyderabad as the host city. Five startups received the BioAsia 2026 Innovation Awards.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: India's retail inflation declined from 4.6% in 2024-25 to approximately what figure in April-December 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Retail inflation declined to 1.7% in April-December 2025-26 from 4.6% in 2024-25. Decline driven by lower prices of vegetables, pulses, and spices.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Chips to Startups (C2S) Programme of the Ministry of Electronics & IT aims to train approximately how many engineers in semiconductor design over the next decade?
questions.explanation: The C2S Programme is an umbrella capacity-building initiative aimed at training about 85,000 engineers in semiconductor design within 10 years.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: How many athletes are being honoured with the Arjuna Award 2026, India's second-highest sporting honour?
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award 2026 honours 24 athletes across various sports disciplines. Hardik Singh (hockey) is the sole Khel Ratna nominee.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which two countries were added to the RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) scheme in April 2026 to support Indian exporters?
questions.explanation: The Government of India expanded the RELIEF scheme by adding Egypt and Jordan as eligible destinations to help Indian exporters navigate logistics disruptions arising from the West Asian conflict.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h and the speed of the stream is 4 km/h. Find the time taken by the boat to go 32 km downstream and return.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 12+4 = 16 km/h. Time = 32/16 = 2 hr. Upstream speed = 12-4 = 8 km/h. Time = 32/8 = 4 hr. Total = 6 hr.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 18 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Area of rhombus = (d1 × d2)/2 = (24 × 18)/2 = 216 cm².
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If the radius of a circle is increased by 25%, by what percentage does its area increase?
questions.explanation: New radius = 1.25r. New area = π(1.25r)² = 1.5625 × original. Increase = 56.25%.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: The average of 8 numbers is 32. If two numbers are added — 40 and 28 — what is the new average?
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: The average of A and B is 35. The average of B and C is 38. The average of A and C is 39. Find A.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: The average mark of 35 students in a class is 60. If a teacher who had a mark of 25 makes a correction and the new average becomes 60.5, find the actual mark of the student.
questions.explanation: Increase in total = 35 × 0.5 = 17.5. So actual mark = 25 + 17.5 = 42.5.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A's salary is 40% more than B's. By what percent is B's salary less than A's?
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If the price of an item rises by 25%, by what percent must consumption fall to keep total expenditure unchanged?
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: In a college of 1,500 students, 60% are boys. If 5% of the boys and 8% of the girls are absent, find the total number of students absent.
questions.explanation: Boys = 900, girls = 600. Absent: 5% × 900 = 45 boys; 8% × 600 = 48 girls. Total = 93.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If 35% of a number is 175, find 60% of the same number.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: In a mixture of 60 L, milk and water are in ratio 7:5. How much water must be removed to make the ratio 7:3?
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If 2A = 3B = 4C, find A : B : C.
questions.explanation: Set 2A=3B=4C=12k. A=6k, B=4k, C=3k. So A:B:C = 6:4:3.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Three friends invest ₹3,000, ₹4,000, ₹5,000 in a partnership and earn a total profit of ₹4,800. Find the share of the second friend.
questions.explanation: Ratio 3:4:5, total parts 12. Second's share = 4/12 × 4800 = 1600.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 5:8. If 8 is added to each, the ratio becomes 7:10. Find the smaller number.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A trader sells two articles each for ₹600. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. Find his net loss percentage.
questions.explanation: Net loss in such cases = (common%/10)² = (20/10)² = 4%.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an item 50% above cost price and gives a 20% discount. Find his profit percentage.
questions.explanation: CP=100, MP=150, SP after 20% discount = 0.8 × 150 = 120. Profit = 20%.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Find the smallest number that when divided by 12, 18, and 24 leaves a remainder of 4 in each case.
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 18, 24) = 72. Smallest number leaving remainder 4 = 72 + 4 = 76.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: If 12 + 12 + 12 + ... (n times) = 12n, find the value of n for which 12n = 144.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Choose the most appropriate word for blank (1).
questions.passage_context: The Indian rupee's exchange rate has long been __(1)__ to global capital flows. In recent years, however, the central bank has __(2)__ a more flexible approach, allowing the currency to find its own level rather than __(3)__ stability through heavy intervention. This shift has not been __(4)__ — exporters and importers have had to plan for greater swings, and policy-makers have had to defend the new framework before sceptical parliamentarians. But, on balance, the policy appears to have __(5)__ India weather a decade of unusual external shocks.
questions.explanation: 'Exposed to global capital flows' is the standard collocation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarizes the author's overall view?
questions.passage_context: India's transition to electric mobility is moving faster than many analysts predicted. Two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and city buses are all logging double-digit market shares for electric variants. Behind this push is a combination of falling battery costs, central-government incentives like FAME-II, and state-level subsidies that vary widely. But the road ahead has potholes. Charging infrastructure remains thin outside major metros, and the financing ecosystem for fleet operators is still nascent. Consumer anxiety about resale value of EVs is another barrier. Industry leaders argue that scaling up will require coordinated action across the central government, states, and private capital — and that the success of India's clean-mobility goals depends on this triangle holding together.
options: EV adoption is failing in India.
EV adoption is moving faster than many predicted, but with real obstacles.
EV adoption requires no further policy intervention.
questions.explanation: The opening line and the 'but the road ahead has potholes' framing capture exactly this.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Identify the segment with an error.

(A) The crowd of fans / (B) were cheering loudly / (C) when the actor / (D) appeared on stage.
questions.explanation: 'Crowd' is a collective noun typically treated as singular when acting as one. So 'was cheering' (singular) is correct, not 'were'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Identify the segment with an error.

(A) She is one of those / (B) who has never been / (C) afraid of speaking the truth / (D) in public.
questions.explanation: 'One of those who...' takes a plural verb because 'who' refers to 'those'. So 'who have never been', not 'who has never been'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form of:

'They will complete the project tomorrow.'
options: The project will be completed by them tomorrow.

questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a meaningful paragraph and identify the SECOND sentence.

(A) Today, those once-rare appearances are commonplace.
(B) The early days of cricket telecasts featured grainy black-and-white footage and limited camera angles.
(C) Live broadcasts were reserved for only the highest-profile matches.
(D) Modern viewers expect ultra-HD streams, multiple commentary feeds, and instant replays.
(E) The shift transformed how millions of fans engaged with the sport.
questions.explanation: B (general past) → C (specific past — only big matches) → A (now commonplace) → D (modern feature) → E (broader implication). 2nd = C.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) Detailed implementation guidelines have already been issued.
(B) The new digital-payments policy was approved last month.
(C) Stakeholder consultations had been held over the previous quarter.
(D) Financial regulators welcomed the move as overdue.
(E) Banks and fintech firms are now adapting their compliance systems.
questions.explanation: C (preceding consultations, past-perfect) → B (policy approved last month) → D (regulators welcomed) → A (guidelines issued) → E (banks adapting now). 1st = C.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I have completed my homework.'

questions.explanation: Past reporting + present-perfect direct → past-perfect indirect. 'I' → 'she'.
